name: Recursive Ray Marching with Early Stopping
definition: A variant of ray marching that dynamically updates the set of active rays (unfinished_mask) at each step, skipping rays that have already hit the surface or exceeded bounds.
summary: Recursive Ray Marching with Early Stopping is a parallelization technique that maintains a dynamic mask to selectively process only unfinished rays, reducing memory and compute overhead compared to naive synchronous batching.
